title: Name produce/consume artifacts by their nature: domain:activity-verb for events, domain:data-noun for state

facts.note: Wagon definition files containing produce/consume blocks are identifiable by path/file kind.
The rule applies both when produce/consume declarations are written and when existing declarations are reviewed or validated; the task/operation type is known from the planning task.

values: existing produce/consume artifact changes nature (event <-> state) or cardinality (single <-> collection) without being renamed
facts.note: Name additions/renames need a diff-level observer on produce[].name / consume[].name; a change of nature or cardinality with an unchanged name needs a diff observer on the artifact's description/contract plus semantic judgement.
Planning tasks that define, change or review wagon interfaces mention these terms.

values: artifact name (new or pre-existing) whose form does not match its nature (event vs state vs collection)
facts.note: Whether a name segment is a past-tense verb, a noun/adjective (including adjective-like participles describing state), or plural, and whether the artifact is really a signal or data, requires linguistic/semantic judgement; no detector exists (implementation.type: none). A pre-existing mismatch found during review triggers the rule just like a new one.

fires: Planner adds a new entry to a wagon's produce block
Planner adds a new entry to a wagon's consume block
Planner renames an existing produce or consume artifact
Planner changes an existing artifact from state to an event (or vice versa) while keeping its name
Planner changes an existing artifact from a single item to a collection (or vice versa) while keeping its name
Planner authors a wagon plan that declares which signals and data the wagon emits or reads
Planner reviews or validates existing produce/consume declarations of a wagon
A review finds a pre-existing produce/consume name whose form does not match the artifact's nature or cardinality
doesNotFire: Editing a wagon manifest for unrelated reasons (e.g. wording-only description edits, WMBT edits) when produce/consume names and artifact nature/cardinality are untouched AND the task is not a review/validation of the interface and no naming mismatch has been found
Naming code-level identifiers (functions, classes, variables) that are not produce/consume artifacts

given: A wagon plan declares a produce block (artifacts the wagon creates and owns) or a consume block (artifacts it consumes).
when: The planner adds, renames, reviews or validates an artifact name there, or changes an artifact's nature (event vs state) or cardinality.
then: Name it domain:activity-verb (past-tense verb) for a signal/event or domain:data-noun (noun/adjective) for state/data, plural for a collection.
prefer: Reuse the producer's exact name on every consume side.
Adjective-like participles describing current state are valid state names (e.g. domain:chosen, domain:remaining); a dotted sub-path after the domain is allowed (e.g. domain:state.current).
avoid: Present/imperative verbs for events; action-describing names for state/data; noun forms for signals.
Singular names for collections; names lacking the 'domain:' prefix.
why: Consistent naming makes an artifact's nature (event vs state vs collection) legible from its name alone, so consumers know whether they react to a signal or read data.
evidence: Every produce[] entry is {name: 'domain:artifact-name', to: 'internal|external'} and every consume[] entry is {name: 'domain:artifact-name', from: 'wagon:slug|system:external|internal'}.

Each signal/event name uses a past-tense activity verb after the domain; each state/data name uses a data noun/adjective (adjective-like participles describing state allowed); each collection is plural.
Reviewer can tell from the name alone whether consumers react to a signal or read data, including for pre-existing artifacts and artifacts whose nature or cardinality changed.
verifier_detail: Naming convention: Events = past tense verbs; State = nouns/adjectives; Collections = plural.
Signal/event pattern: domain:activity-verb (source examples: match:started, pacing:exhausted). State/data pattern: domain:data-noun (source examples: player:identity, match:config).

Source positive examples (naming_convention): 'match:started' (activity-verb pattern for signal); 'pacing:exhausted' (activity-verb signal); 'player:identity' (data-noun pattern for state); 'match:config' (data-noun state).

Produce block shape: array of {name: 'domain:artifact-name', to: 'internal|external'}; lists artifacts the wagon creates and owns, with visibility specified via 'to'. Planner prompt: 'What artifacts does this wagon create and own? Specify visibility with 'to'. Follow naming pattern: domain:activity-verb for signals/events, domain:data-noun for state/data'.

Source produce positive examples: 'decision:chosen, to external' (data-noun pattern); 'match:started, to external' (activity-verb pattern for signal); 'player:identity, to external' (data-noun pattern for state).

Consume block shape: array of {name: 'domain:artifact-name', from: 'wagon:slug|system:external|internal'}; lists artifacts the wagon consumes. Planner prompt: 'What artifacts does this wagon consume? Follow naming pattern: domain:activity-verb for signals/events, domain:data-noun for state/data'.

Source consume positive examples: 'match:dilemma.current, from wagon:pace-dilemmas' (data-noun; dotted sub-path after the domain is allowed); 'time:remaining, from wagon:burn-timebank' (data-noun); 'match:started, from wagon:play-match' (activity-verb signal, same name as on the producer side); 'player:identity, from system:external' (data-noun from external train).

Note: the source labels 'decision:chosen' and 'time:remaining' as data-noun names even though they are participles; classify by meaning: an adjective-like participle describing current state/data is a data-noun name, a past-tense verb reporting that something happened is an event name.
No mechanical detector exists (implementation.type: none); classification is LLM/reviewer judged.

additions.text: The produce/consume block structure (creates-and-owns vs consumes, array entry shape, 'to' visibility, 'from' source) is an independent obligation from naming; propose planner.interface.produce-consume-shape. additions.justification: Rule 2: one obligation per convention, without dropping planner-facing guidance.

additions.text: Reuse the producer's exact name on every consume side.
additions.justification: Implied by the source examples (the same names appear identically on produce and consume sides); stated explicitly so planners don't drift names across wagons. No ordering/workflow instruction is added.

additions.justification: Derived from the source's own positive examples (S030, S040, S041); surfaced in planner-facing guidance so planners do not reject valid participle state names, generalized to avoid carrying application-specific vocabulary into generic guidance.

additions.justification: The source only gives positive patterns; anti-patterns are their direct inverses, phrased semantically so they do not contradict participle state names. No new obligation.
